footer.data: Klar is itself an AI system, and tells you so on every screen. Your descriptions stay in your own anonymous session and are deleted after 30 days without activity. Models are reached through OpenRouter; embeddings run on an EU host. Full list of providers in the privacy notice.

welcome.title: Let's see where your AI tools stand.
welcome.intro: Add the tools your company uses, one at a time. Klar checks each one in the AI Act's order, cites every step, and builds your to-do list with dates.

profile.heading: About your company
profile.subtitle: Takes a minute. You can change it later. It doesn't change how your tools are classified.
profile.establishedHint: Established outside the EU? The Act still applies when your tools' output is used in the EU (Art. 2(1)(c)), and a provider of high-risk systems appoints a representative in the EU (Art. 22).
profile.usedInHint: The Act applies to AI used in the EU, wherever the provider sits (Art. 2).

label.none: Neither an SME nor a small mid-cap

body.sme: SMEs get lighter documentation duties, and the lower of the two maximum fines applies to them (Art. 99(6)), not the higher one of Art. 99(3).
body.smc: For a small mid-cap, the lower of the two maximum fines applies to fines under Art. 99(4) and (5) (Art. 99(6a)), but not to breaches of the Art. 5 bans (Art. 99(3)). Small mid-caps may use the simplified documentation too (Art. 11(1)).
body.none: Neither the relief for SMEs (Art. 99(6)) nor the one for small mid-caps (Art. 99(6a)) applies, so the higher of the two maximum fines applies (Art. 99(3) to (5)).
body.noneOriginal: The relief for SMEs (Art. 99(6)) doesn't apply, so the higher of the two maximum fines applies (Art. 99(3) to (5)). The original 2024 text has no small mid-cap rules.

size.maybeSme: Klar looks at turnover only. With a balance sheet total of up to €43 m you may still count as an SME.
size.maybeSmc: Klar looks at turnover only. With a balance sheet total of up to €129 m you may still count as a small mid-cap.

art99_3.quote: Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

art99_6.quote: In the case of SMEs, including start-ups, each fine referred to in this Article shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, whichever thereof is lower.

art2_1_c.quote: providers and deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located in a third country, where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union;

art22_1.quote: Prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.

art99_6a.quote: In the case of SMCs, each fine referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 shall be up to the percentages or amount referred therein, whichever is lower.

legacy.legacy_unchanged: Art. 111(2): the tool was on the market or in use before {{date}}, so the marked high-risk duties apply only if its design or intended purpose changes significantly. The class stays high-risk.
legacy.legacy_public_authority: Art. 111(2): the tool was on the market or in use before {{date}} and is meant for public authorities, so the marked high-risk duties apply from {{deadline}}. The class stays high-risk.
legacy.perProduct: This covers copies placed on the market or put into service before {{date}}; copies supplied on or after that date may be fully covered.

question.ifNoText: Not high-risk on this point. The transparency check then decides whether any duties apply.

todo.heading: What you need to do

intro.provider: The tool is placed on the market or put into service under your name, so the duties for building, documenting and monitoring it are yours.
intro.deployer: You didn't build the tool, so most technical duties sit with its provider. As the company using it, you must use it as instructed, keep people in charge of it, and tell staff and the people it affects.
intro.importer: You bring the tool into the EU, so you check that its provider did its part before you sell it (Art. 23).
intro.distributor: You pass the tool on, so you check that it carries the required marking and documents before you do (Art. 24).

todo.minimal: No specific duties for this tool. One general duty applies to every company that uses AI:
todo.limited: Tell people they're dealing with AI. Klar drafts the disclosure for you.
todo.none: No duties are listed for this result.
